To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the intrinsic electrophysiology of a given hippocampal cell type can be achieved by multiple combinations of ion channels with different densities, and that the set of channels expressed in any given neuron can be partitioned in two subsets: one responsible for the major electrophysiological characteristics of the neuron, and another responsible for robust degeneracy among the different combinations.

(1) the set of conductance densities expressed in a given neuron is highly variable and (2) there are two subsets of these conductances that are responsible for the variability in the firing behavior of the neuron and for the variability in firing properties across the population, respectively.
the intrinsic electrophysiology of hippocampal neurons is highly variable, but that this variability is degenerate and robust.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of biologically accurate computational models of hippocampally-derived neurons, and their use to explore the mechanisms underlying the intrinsic variability of ion channel densities in the brain.

the question of how a given set of ion channels can be combined in order to produce a wide repertoire of neuronal firing patterns in a network of morphologically and electrophysiologically realistic neurons.

the development of a unified data-driven workflow for building biophysically realistic models of hippocampally-derived neurons and with the use of these models to explore the mechanisms of channel degeneracy and their role in shaping neuronal input/output functions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the variability in the expression of ion channels in hippocampal pyramidal and interneurons may be explained by a degenerate set of conductances that are robust to changes in their relative expression levels.

degeneracy in the channel composition is a fundamental feature of the intrinsic electrophysiology of hippocampal neurons, but that it is also highly constrained by the need of each neuron to fulfill its specific role in the circuit.
the expression of a particular combination of ion channels in a given neuron is not random but follows a set of rules that are still to be determined.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the degeneracy among the different conductances in a neuron is not random, but rather is highly structured, and this structure may be used by the neuron to achieve its functional goals.

, although the intrinsic properties of hippocampal pyramidal cells are more variable than those of interneurons, the set of ion channels expressed in both populations is degenerate, and the degeneracy is stronger than the variability.
the variability in the peak conductance of ion channel types in hippocampal pyramidal neurons is much larger than the variability in the total peak conductance of the neuron.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the degeneracy of ion channel expression is an essential feature of hippocampal neuronal physiology, and should be taken into account in future modeling studies of the hippocampal circuitry.
the degeneracy in the channel composition of individual neurons is not random, but rather follows a pattern that is consistent with the role of each type of neuron in the circuit.

the degeneracy in the expression of ion channel conductances in hippocampal neurons may be the result of a trade-off between robustness of the firing behavior and flexibility in the expression of conductances.
